lesson_ops.text: Repository-adaptive inventory and ranked localization improve cross-repository task success, especially when package layout, test conventions, and entry points vary.
Explicit contracts, invariants, compatibility constraints, and acceptance criteria improve fixes by exposing project-specific edge cases before editing.
A completion contract improves reporting discipline by requiring a diff, reproducer, regression result, and criterion check before claiming success.
Tracing values across normalization, mutation, serialization, and exception boundaries improves fixes for edge-case failures by exposing where behavior diverges from the intended invariant.
Ranked hypotheses paired with minimal discriminating probes improve difficult fixes by reducing incorrect edits and increasing implementation confidence.
Bounded diagnosis with recovery checkpoints improves difficult-task completion by enabling test-guided retries, while uncapped retries can waste budget or reinforce incorrect hypotheses.
Executable boundary, invalid-input, stateful, and mutation tests, including a direct regression check and nearby compatibility check, improve detection of incomplete or overbroad fixes.

Transactional patching with checkpointed full-diff and preflight validation improves output integrity by catching truncated, unintended, syntactically invalid, or path/mode-corrupt changes before submission.

lesson_ops.text: Strict validation that edit plans are complete and non-empty improves patch application accuracy, especially on malformed or partial model-generated commands.
Scanning raw responses and fenced code regions for decodable JSON improves robustness when model outputs are malformed or wrapped in extra text.
Preserving the multi-file edit-command path improves repairs that require coordinated changes across multiple files.
Broadening localization with symbols, call relationships, tests, tracebacks, and definitions improves target alignment and repair quality on difficult probes.
Decomposing repairs with causal chains, explicit invariants, and acceptance criteria improves technical grounding and repair quality beyond basic localization checklists.
Forcing model temperature to zero improves execution repeatability and output-schema adherence, but does not improve evidence-based fault localization.
Extracting unified diffs from model prose improves patch application when valid patches are wrapped in explanatory text, though it remains less reliable for multi-file or ambiguous diff content.

Normalizing patch payloads by removing BOM and surrounding whitespace, accepting common fences, and enforcing consistent line endings with a trailing newline improves recovery and application reliability.
Rejecting no-op and syntactically unappliable patches before orchestration improves reliability by catching generation failures early, though overly strict whitespace checks can reject valid patches.
Requiring explicit minimal-change scope, forbidden changes, and expected behavior in repair plans improves response discipline and orchestration robustness.
Accepting JSON envelopes that directly contain patches or diffs improves patch application when models return structured patch payloads instead of raw unified diffs.
Providing a ranked context bundle containing the failing path, relevant definitions, callers, overrides, fixtures, and analogous tests improves retrieval alignment and repair quality.

lesson_ops.text: Explicitly mapping requirements to code branches and focused before/after tests strongly improves validation and reduces missed behavioral regressions.
Requirement-to-code traceability tables plus bidirectional repository-graph analysis improve localization and caller/callee coverage.
Repository changes that hard-code token estimation, malformed-input policies, timeouts, retries, or narrow APIs without repository-specific evidence tend to harm correctness.
Differential reproduction tests that demonstrate the pre-patch failure and post-patch fix provide stronger regression protection than generic behavioral checks alone.

A gated requirements-evidence-plan-edit-validation protocol improves repository-fix correctness more than unstructured implementation, especially when it requires explicit evidence before editing and targeted validation afterward.

Requiring explicit edge cases, unchanged-neighbor behavior, requirement-to-branch mappings, and rejection conditions in implementation plans improves patch completeness and reduces missed behavioral constraints.
Normalizing line endings and removing only an outer Markdown fence from generated patches improves patch applicability while preserving patch content.
Requiring repository-wide searches, per-file evidence, and differential localization around the smallest failing path improves fix localization and reduces symptom-level or wrong-file edits.
